reporting_requirement.when: After each implemented or materially updated screen, before switching workspace or final handoff.
reporting_requirement.rule:
## Haspataal: required progress reporting

Use this repository's Haspataal MCP connection (haspataal_project in Codex,
haspataal in other agents). At the start of every session, call my_progress and
progress_proposals for the connected implementation. Read returned review feedback.
Read overview and get_guide('connecting-your-coding-agent') for the full backend
workflow; use get_screen_bundle and get_ui_quality_brief before building each screen.

After implementing or materially updating any screen, submit propose_progress
without waiting for the developer to ask. Do this before moving to another
workspace or giving your final handoff. A workspace needs a separate proposal
for every screen with newly implemented, tested rubric items.

Use the current rubric fingerprint and item IDs from get_screen_bundle/my_progress,
the connected implementation_id, the tested commit or identifiable build, and
readable Markdown evidence: changed files, checks run and results, and limitations.
Report only items actually implemented and tested. Partial work is reportable;
leave untested items out and describe missing human review honestly. Never invent
test results, a human review or approval.

The human tester records each workspace's review on the portal. Build the DEV-only
Review code setting (get_ui_quality_brief: dev_build_headers): one app-wide field in
Settings -> This terminal, whose code the shared API client sends as X-Haspataal-Review.
Keep it and the X-Haspataal-* headers behind the DEV build flag (compiled out of release
builds). Never set a code yourself, in tests or scripts. progress_proposals returns the
signed reviews' failures: fix them.

First check accepted claims and progress_proposals: do not resubmit unchanged work
already accepted or awaiting review. Reuse the same request_id and identical payload
when retrying a lost response; use a new request_id for changed evidence or a new build.
Verify the saved proposal with progress_proposals. In your handoff, name the proposal
IDs and say "awaiting human review on /docs -> My progress".

If submission fails, keep the exact payload and request_id in the repository without
credentials, report the blocker, and retry at the next session. Never say progress
was posted until the server confirms it. If no item is ready, explain why; do not
submit empty or invented claims merely to satisfy this rule.

Proposals earn no points. Only the human's authenticated portal review can accept
claims; agents must never approve their own proposals or nominate an implementation.

report_on: Agents must submit propose_progress after each implemented screen; the human reviews these on /docs -> My progress. Only accepted items count. Manual human reporting remains available.

answered_since_last_read.title: Waste collected before contractor arrival has no supported later-handover operation
answered_since_last_read.response: Confirmed, and thank you for refusing to record the same weight twice: that was the right call. A waste record could take its consignment note only at the collection; nothing attached one later. From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) POST /infection/waste/handover {waste_ids, vendor_id, manifest_number, disposal, handed_over_on (default today)} attaches one consignment note to the collections it covers, each handed over whole and once: the weight is never entered again. Its permission is the one that records waste (infection.waste.record), and both waste_log and waste_log_ops list it (one new endpoint item each on your checklist; no approved rule was reworded). Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry after a lost answer gets the same answer; sent again without it, the collections are refused. (2) The answer: the contractor, the note, the disposal, the day, weight_kg (the sum of the collections it covers) and the records. (3) Refusals: WASTE_HANDED_OVER (409, new: a collection already carries a note; details.waste_id, manifest_number, handed_over_on; it is final), REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND (details.field waste_ids with the unknown ids, or vendor_id), VALIDATION_ERROR (a handover in the future, or before a collection's day). (4) GET /infection/waste?awaiting_handover=true lists the collections no note covers yet, however old: the screen's handover picker. Each record now carries handed_over_on and handed_over_by_name (null while it waits), and the totals' handed_over_kg follow. (5) The database keeps it so: a collection never changes once recorded, and a consignment note is final once attached; one given at the collection (POST /infection/waste with vendor_id) is dated that day. A collection is handed over whole, never in part: bags that leave on different days are weighed as separate collections. The infection-control playbook, both screens' bundles and the description of POST /infection/waste say so. This update changes the migrations, so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays) and your synthetic waste_id 1 is gone. To check it: as demo.ops record two synthetic collections without a contractor; GET /infection/waste?awaiting_handover=true lists them; POST /infection/waste/handover with both, a contractor from GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=Contractor and a synthetic note: 200, weight_kg their sum; the same again without a key: 409 WASTE_HANDED_OVER; the totals' handed_over_kg equal their weight_kg.

answered_since_last_read.title: Equipment screen bundles omit the existing vendor lookup needed for contractor fields
answered_since_last_read.response: Confirmed, and thank you for checking that the route works and that no duplicate was open: it is exactly a catalogue gap. Both equipment screens take vendor ids (supplier_vendor_id and service_vendor_id on PUT /facility/equipment/{asset_id}; vendor_id on a contractor's plan and visit) but did not list the directory they come from. Checking every screen the same way found three more forms in the same position: equipment requisitions (an option's vendor_id), the operations console (a work order's contractor, a utility bill's provider) and lab administration (PUT /lab/contractor contractor_vendor_id). From fixed_in on (compare overview's server_build with fixed_in): (1) GET /finance/vendors is listed by equipment_maintenance, equipment_maintenance_ops, equipment_requisitions, ops_console and lab_admin, so get_screen_bundle, generate_typescript(kind=screen) and screen_test_plan of each include it. (2) The route has a description now: the directory every vendor picker reads, open to any logged-in user; filter by vendor_type (Contractor, EquipmentSupplier, UtilityProvider, ...) and offer the active ones (is_active); finance adds a vendor with POST /finance/vendors. vendor_type is a typed value list now, so an unknown type answers 422 VALIDATION_ERROR instead of an empty list. (3) Each vendor field of those forms names the directory in its description, as category_id names GET /ops/utility-categories. (4) The playbooks facility-compliance-equipment-drills, facility-and-it and laboratory-and-radiology say where each vendor is picked. (5) A backend test fails on any screen whose form takes a vendor id without listing GET /finance/vendors. No response field changed. Your checklist gains one endpoint item on each of those five screens; no approved rule was reworded. This build also carries the fix of #53, which changes the migrations, so the DEV server is reinstalled with fresh hospital data (your registry account stays). To check it: get_screen_bundle for equipment_maintenance and equipment_maintenance_ops lists GET /finance/vendors; generate_typescript(kind=screen, name=equipment_maintenance) has its function; as demo.maintenance GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=Contractor answers the contractors, and ?vendor_type=Plumber answers 422. (6) This build goes further (decision 62, commit 7429acf): checking every screen for the same gap found 86 screens whose forms take other ids from lists their bundles did not name (departments, wards, staff, patients, stays, medicines and their batches, assets, theatres and more). Each now lists its directory, each field's description names it, and the test of (5) covers every such id, except those the backend wrote down with a reason (the record the form is opened on, or an id the owner chose to leave without a picker). GET /staff/lookup also answers user_id (null without a login) for the fields that name a user; the bed matrix (its wards, without patient names), GET /ot/theaters and GET /ops/assets (without the purchase cost and date) are open to the screens that pick from them; the Quality Officer may read the formulary; GET /lab/reagents/{reagent_id}/batches is new. Your checklist gains 139 more items (138 endpoints and one rule on report_incident), none reworded. The update note lists every screen and what your app should do.
